text:
sara_support: FYI customer #8421 reporting Private deployment in their VPC lost healthchecks after a DX maintenance window. API calls return 502/timeout from their side. Ticket 8421-PRIV created.
customer_dev: seeing TLS handshake errors in their logs: "tls: handshake failure" and repeated IKE rekeys. Started after the DX maintenance at ~02:10 UTC.
james_neteng: can you paste the vpn/peer config and BGP session status? suspect route learning issue or BGP flap.
sara_support: quick dump attached in case, but here's the error snippets they quoted: ```Jun 12 02:11:02 vpn[1234]: IKEv2: CHILD_SA rekey failed: AUTH_FAILED
Jun 12 02:11:21 kernel: skb: dropped packet from 10.0.3.12 -> 54.239.16.1 (DF)
```
customer_dev: BGP shows Established for a few minutes then resets, peers are not learning the private subnets. Route table empty.
tim_sre: can we get a tcpdump from their VPC NAT gateway and our egress nodes? also need the IKE SA debug from the customer's CPE side (pre-shared key ok?).
customer_dev: they confirmed PSK unchanged. I forwarded IKE logs showing peer sending Notify payload with CERTIFICATE_FAILED shortly before retries.
james_neteng: CERTIFICATE_FAILED suggests our cert chain might be blocked or OCSP stapling failing. Are we allowing outbound 443 to OCSP responders from the Private control plane? customer is in a locked-down egress allowlist.
sara_support: customer says their egress allowlist is only to our IPs and AWS DX endpoints, nothing external. They whitelist our control-plane IPs but not ocsp.responder.*.
chris_oncall: ops-bot pulled recent deploys: no cert rotation pushes in the last 24h. However, one health-probe change changed which proxy egress node is used for that tenant. Could be hitting a node with more restrictive NAT config.
james_neteng: quick repro: from a restricted VPC that only allows our control-plane IPs, try TLS handshake to our gateway while blocking OCSP/CRL. Most TLS stacks will still handshake, but if client enforces cert revocation and we rely on stapled OCSP, handshake could fail. Also IKE with certificate verification will fail if CA chain or OCSP not reachable.
tim_sre: suggested immediate customer workaround: allow outbound 443 to the following OCSP/CDN ranges (we provided list in ticket) OR temporarily disable OCSP verification on their CPE to restore tunnels while we investigate. Also suggest adding our fallback peering route to their VPC routing as a short-term traffic path.
sara_support: customer asked for concrete steps. I sent: 1) Add egress rule: allow TCP/443 to ocsp1.example-ca.com (and CDN ranges) 2) Restart IKE session on their CPE 3) Verify BGP routes.
customer_dev: performed step 1 and 2, BGP resumed, routes learned, API calls from their app recovered. They report reduced 502s.
james_neteng: follow-ups: we should audit our egress nodes to ensure OCSP endpoints reachable from all proxy nodes, and add healthcheck for OCSP reachability per-tenant so we can alert earlier.
chris_oncall: opened infra-issue #ISS-1197 to add OCSP probes and map tenants to egress node. tagging @eng-infra for NAT config checks.
sara_support: closing loop with customer, documenting workaround in ticket 8421-PRIV. Will keep thread here for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Deploybot: no config deploys affecting VPN certs in last 48h.
tim_sre: next steps: (a) infra to verify all egress proxies have NAT rules for OCSP/CDN ranges; (b) product to consider fallbacks when OCSP unreachable during IKE; (c) support to add checklist for Private deployments during DX maint windows.
sara_support: thanks all — customer confirmed full recovery at 02:48 UTC. I'll mark resolved but request postmortem due to cross-team impact.
